newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian tin down to new 27-month low.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian tin down to new 27-month low.

text.p: Malaysia's tin price ended three cents lower to a new 27-month low of 13.67 ringgit ($5.42) a kg on Wednesday after selling by players tracking an overnight fall on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
They said the price could rise to 13.75 ringgit by the end of this week if the LME strengthened.
"The problem with the LME now is that it's weak, and that's why buying only came in at the lower level this morning," said a tin trader in Malaysia.
There were initial offers for 134 tonnes of tin on Wednesday, compared to bids of 62 tonnes.
Final turnover was 119 tonnes, against 128 on Tuesday. Buyers were from Europe, Japan and Malaysia and the local premium against London rose rose to $45 from $15 previously.
